name: Horizontal Push
description: Pressing a load away from the torso in the horizontal/transverse plane, driven by shoulder horizontal adduction and elbow extension. Prime movers: pectoralis major (sternal/clavicular heads), anterior deltoid, triceps. Exemplars: flat/incline barbell and dumbbell bench press, machine chest press, push-up, cable fly. Bench inclination shifts emphasis from sternal pec (flat) toward clavicular pec and anterior deltoid (incline).

name: Horizontal Pull
description: Drawing a load toward the torso in the horizontal/transverse plane via shoulder horizontal abduction/extension and elbow flexion. Prime movers: mid-trapezius, rhomboids, posterior deltoid, latissimus dorsi, with biceps/brachialis assisting. Exemplars: barbell/dumbbell row, seated cable row, chest-supported row, prone bench pull, inverted row.

name: Vertical Push (Overhead Press)
description: Pressing a load overhead, primarily shoulder flexion/abduction plus upward scapular rotation and elbow extension. Prime movers: anterior and lateral deltoid, upper trapezius, serratus anterior, triceps. Exemplars: standing/seated overhead barbell press, dumbbell shoulder press, machine shoulder press, push press, Arnold press.

name: Vertical Pull
description: Pulling a load downward from overhead toward the torso via shoulder adduction/extension, downward scapular rotation, and elbow flexion. Prime movers: latissimus dorsi, teres major, lower trapezius, rhomboids, with biceps/brachialis assisting. Exemplars: pull-up, chin-up, lat pulldown (wide/neutral/supinated), straight-arm pulldown, lat prayer.

name: Hip Hinge
description: Flexing and extending at the hip with a relatively fixed, neutral spine and minimal knee travel, loading the posterior chain through a long hip moment arm. Prime movers: gluteus maximus and hamstrings (acting at the hip), with erector spinae resisting trunk flexion isometrically. Exemplars: conventional/Romanian/stiff-leg deadlift, good morning, kettlebell swing.

name: Squat (Knee-Dominant Bilateral)
description: Simultaneous hip and knee flexion/extension under axial or anterior load with the trunk relatively upright, emphasizing the quadriceps with substantial gluteus maximus and adductor contribution. Exemplars: back squat (high/low bar), front squat, hack squat, leg press, goblet squat, belt squat.

name: Lunge / Split Squat (Unilateral Knee-Dominant)
description: Single-leg or staggered-stance hip-and-knee flexion/extension that loads one limb at a time while demanding frontal/transverse-plane stability. Prime movers: quadriceps and gluteus maximus of the lead leg, with adductors and gluteus medius stabilizing. Exemplars: forward/reverse/walking lunge, static split squat, Bulgarian split squat, step-up.

name: Knee Flexion (Leg Curl)
description: Isolated flexion of the knee against resistance, training the hamstrings in their knee-flexor role (distinct from their hip-extensor role in the hinge). Prime movers: biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus, with gastrocnemius and popliteus assisting. Exemplars: lying, seated, and standing leg curl; Nordic ham curl; glute-ham raise. Hip position (seated vs lying) modulates hamstring length and regional emphasis.

name: Knee Extension (Leg Extension)
description: Isolated extension of the knee against resistance, training the quadriceps independent of the hip. Prime movers: rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius. Exemplars: machine leg extension; hip/torso angle and a small lengthened-position tweak can bias the rectus femoris and alter regional growth.

name: Plantarflexion, Knee Straight (Gastrocnemius)
description: Ankle plantarflexion performed with the knee extended, which keeps the biarticular gastrocnemius at length and makes it the primary contributor (alongside the soleus). Exemplars: standing calf raise, leg-press calf raise (legs straight), donkey calf raise.

name: Plantarflexion, Knee Bent (Soleus)
description: Ankle plantarflexion performed with the knee flexed (~90 degrees), which shortens and slackens the gastrocnemius and shifts the load onto the monoarticular soleus. Exemplars: seated calf raise, bent-knee leg-press calf raise.

name: Elbow Flexion, Supinated (Biceps Curl)
description: Elbow flexion with the forearm supinated, maximizing biceps brachii involvement (which both flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm). Exemplars: barbell/dumbbell/EZ-bar curl, preacher curl, incline curl, cable curl. The neutral- and pronated-grip variants are tracked as separate patterns because they shift load toward the brachialis/brachioradialis.

name: Elbow Flexion, Neutral (Hammer / Brachialis)
description: Elbow flexion with the forearm in neutral (thumbs-up) grip, which reduces the biceps' mechanical advantage and biases the brachialis and brachioradialis. Exemplars: hammer curl, neutral-grip cable/dumbbell curl, cross-body hammer curl.

name: Elbow Flexion, Pronated (Reverse Curl / Brachioradialis)
description: Elbow flexion with the forearm pronated (palms-down), which slackens the biceps and emphasizes the brachioradialis and wrist/forearm extensors. Exemplars: reverse barbell/EZ-bar curl, reverse preacher curl.

name: Elbow Extension (Triceps)
description: Extension of the elbow against resistance, isolating the triceps brachii. Shoulder position changes which head is emphasized: overhead positions lengthen and bias the long head, while arm-at-side positions favor the lateral/medial heads. Exemplars: cable pushdown, overhead extension (EZ-bar/cable/dumbbell), skull-crusher, dip, close-grip bench press, kickback.

name: Shoulder Abduction (Lateral Raise)
description: Raising the arm away from the midline in the frontal plane, training the lateral (and supraspinatus/anterior) deltoid in its abductor role. Exemplars: dumbbell/cable/machine lateral raise, leaning cable lateral raise, upright row (wider grip). Distinct from horizontal abduction, which targets the posterior deltoid.

name: Shoulder Horizontal Abduction (Rear Delt)
description: Moving the arm backward away from the midline in the transverse plane with the arm elevated ~90 degrees, isolating the posterior deltoid (with mid-trap/rhomboid assistance). Exemplars: reverse pec-deck, bent-over/seated rear-delt dumbbell fly, cable rear-delt fly, face pull. It is the direct opposite of the horizontal-push (shoulder horizontal adduction) action.

name: Shoulder Flexion (Front Raise)
description: Raising the arm forward and up in the sagittal plane, training the anterior deltoid (with clavicular pec assistance) in its flexor role. Exemplars: dumbbell/barbell/cable/plate front raise. Heavily overlapped by vertical and incline pressing, so often a low-priority accessory.

name: Wrist Flexion
description: Flexing the wrist against resistance to train the anterior forearm flexor compartment (flexor carpi radialis/ulnaris, palmaris longus, and the finger flexors). Exemplars: seated/standing wrist curl (barbell or dumbbell), behind-the-back wrist curl. Closely related to crushing grip work.

name: Wrist Extension
description: Extending the wrist against resistance to train the posterior forearm extensor compartment (extensor carpi radialis longus/brevis, extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor digitorum). Exemplars: reverse wrist curl, wrist roller (extension phase). Often paired with reverse curls for forearm balance.

name: Hip Abduction
description: Moving the femur away from the midline in the frontal plane, training the gluteus medius/minimus and upper gluteus maximus fibers. Exemplars: machine hip abduction, cable/banded standing abduction, side-lying abduction, banded lateral walk. Contributes to frontal-plane pelvic stability in single-leg work.

name: Hip Extension (Glute-Dominant)
description: Extension of the femur relative to the pelvis with limited knee involvement, emphasizing the gluteus maximus near full extension where its moment arm peaks. Exemplars: barbell hip thrust, glute bridge, cable pull-through, 45-degree back/hip extension, reverse hyperextension, kickback. Distinguished from the hinge by its horizontal load vector and shorter spinal-erector demand.

name: Spinal Flexion (Trunk Flexion / Crunch)
description: Concentric flexion of the lumbar/thoracic spine (and/or hip flexion drawing the pelvis toward the ribcage) against resistance, training the rectus abdominis and hip flexors. Exemplars: crunch, cable crunch, weighted sit-up, hanging/lying leg raise, reverse crunch, machine ab crunch.

name: Anti-Rotation (Trunk Stability)
description: Isometrically resisting an externally applied rotational (transverse-plane) torque to keep the trunk square, training the obliques and deep core as anti-rotators. Exemplars: Pallof press, anti-rotation cable hold, single-arm farmer carry (resisting twist), bird-dog. A stability pattern with no direct concentric antagonist.

name: Anti-Extension (Trunk Stability)
description: Isometrically resisting lumbar extension to maintain a braced, neutral spine against a force that would arch the back, training the rectus abdominis and deep core anteriorly. Exemplars: front plank, ab-wheel rollout, body saw, hollow-body hold, dead bug. A stability pattern with no direct concentric antagonist.

name: Anti-Lateral-Flexion (Trunk Stability)
description: Isometrically resisting frontal-plane side-bending to keep the trunk vertical under an asymmetric load, training the quadratus lumborum and obliques. Exemplars: suitcase carry, single-arm farmer carry, side plank, standing single-arm overhead hold. A stability pattern with no direct concentric antagonist.

name: Loaded Carry
description: Locomotion while holding an external load, integrating grip endurance, trunk bracing (anti-flexion/lateral-flexion/rotation depending on load placement), postural stability, and gait. Exemplars: farmer's walk, suitcase carry, front-rack carry, overhead carry, yoke walk. Whole-body in nature, so no single antagonist pattern.
